event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an interstate conflict rooted in Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine, which expanded into a full-scale Russian armed attack on 24 February 2022. It has involved combat and long-range strikes across Ukraine and, increasingly, attacks affecting Russian territory, alongside major humanitarian, legal, diplomatic and economic consequences.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: In March 2014, the UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, and declared that the 16 March 2014 Crimea referendum could not alter Crimea’s status.

facts.label: Full-scale phase
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission says Russian armed forces launched a full-scale armed attack on Ukraine on 24 February 2022; this is the date generally used for the war’s current large-scale phase.

facts.label: Parties and geography
facts.value: The core belligerents are the Russian Federation and Ukraine. The International Court of Justice’s 16 March 2022 provisional-measures order referred to Russian military operations begun on 24 February 2022 “in the territory of Ukraine.”

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution ES-11/1, demanding that Russia immediately cease its use of force against Ukraine and withdraw its military forces; the resolution also called for a peaceful resolution through dialogue, negotiations and mediation.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: UN human-rights monitoring has documented extensive civilian harm, displacement and damage to homes, medical and educational facilities, and critical infrastructure; it cautions that verified civilian-casualty totals understate the actual toll where access and verification are limited.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows a limited set of late-July to mid-August 2026 developments, including cross-border strikes, reported casualties and humanitarian findings; it does not provide a comprehensive military, diplomatic or legal history of the war.

explore_lenses.title: A narrow humanitarian truce expired without extension
explore_lenses.summary: The six-day Oleshky-area pause was a localized arrangement for evacuation, demining and aid delivery, not a nationwide ceasefire. It ended late on November 1 after both sides reported no violations there, while strikes continued elsewhere in Ukraine.

claims.text: The Oleshky ceasefire enabled evacuations and delivery of food and medical supplies; Ukrainian and Russian officials reported no violations during the six-day pause.
Ukraine's military said it evacuated 167 people from threatened parts of Kherson region on November 1, including 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility.

A Ukrainian official told AFP that Russia declined Ukraine's proposal to extend the local ceasefire; the Kremlin described the Oleshky operation and cooperation between the countries' human-rights commissioners positively.
The aid-centre strike occurred after the Oleshky truce expired, but the available reporting does not establish that the expiration caused or directly enabled the attack in neighboring Zaporizhzhia.

explore_lenses.label: What made the journey an unbroken route?
explore_lenses.title: Two rules shaped the expedition
explore_lenses.summary: Bushby defined the Goliath Expedition by continuity rather than simply distance: he would not use transport to advance and would not return home until arriving on foot. That framework required him to find non-motorized ways across barriers normally bypassed by travelers.

claims.text: Bushby’s expedition website states its two rules were “no transport to advance” and no going home except on foot; it says he regarded them as unbroken throughout the journey.
The final stages included a 288-kilometre Caspian Sea crossing in 2024 and a swim of the English Channel that brought him to Dover on October 5, 2026.
Bushby characterized the accomplishment as collective, crediting help from strangers, family, friends and governments rather than portraying it as a solely individual feat.

explore_lenses.title: Borders, financing and rerouting prolonged it
explore_lenses.summary: The duration was driven not only by terrain and physical danger, but by access and logistical constraints. Visa denials, restricted borders, changing geopolitics, the pandemic and lost sponsorship repeatedly stopped or altered the route.

claims.text: Associated Press reported that Bushby originally expected a 12-year trek, but visa issues and weather alone meant nearly 10 years navigating Russia; a 2012 visa refusal prompted a 5,600-kilometre protest walk from Los Angeles to the Russian Embassy in Washington.

Bushby’s expedition account says that, after routes through Iran, Turkmenistan and Russia became unavailable amid sanctions, the pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the team chose the Caspian Sea crossing as an alternative.
AP reported that the 2008 financial crisis cost Bushby sponsors, while later support from a production company helped sustain the expedition.

story_report.summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby has completed a 28-year journey that began in Punta Arenas, Chile, on November 1, 1998. He traveled about 50,000 kilometers across four continents and 30 countries before returning to his mother’s home in Hull, ending a trek that took him through jungles and frozen seas. The reunion with his family brought the long-running expedition to a close.

sections.heading: Bushby’s Rules Defined the Expedition
sections.body: Bushby’s expedition website says the journey followed two self-imposed rules: no transport could be used to advance, and he could not return home except on foot. The site says he considered both rules unbroken. Its final stages included a 288-kilometre Caspian Sea crossing in 2024 and a swim across the English Channel, reaching Dover on October 5, 2026. Bushby has described the achievement as collective, crediting strangers, relatives, friends and governments for their help.

sections.heading: Visas, Weather and Funding Extended Trek
sections.body: Bushby originally expected the journey to take 12 years, but Associated Press reported that visa difficulties and weather alone led to nearly 10 years navigating Russia. After a visa refusal in 2012, he undertook a 5,600-kilometre protest walk from Los Angeles to the Russian Embassy in Washington. The 2008 financial crisis also cost him sponsors, although later backing from a production company helped sustain the expedition. When routes through Iran, Turkmenistan and Russia became unavailable, his team selected the Caspian crossing as an alternative.

sections.heading: Bushby Plans Tour as Documentary Develops

Before arriving home, Bushby said ending the mission could make it difficult to re-enter a society he no longer knew; a spokesperson said he did not know what would come next.

event_overview.title: About Cybersecurity Incident
event_overview.subject: Cybersecurity Incident
event_overview.summary: This event is a series of suspected cyber intrusions into internet-connected commercial refrigeration controls, first reported in French food retail stores in mid-October 2026 and followed by similar disruptions elsewhere in Europe. The incidents caused refrigeration and freezer settings to change, forcing retailers to isolate equipment and discard food that could no longer be kept safely chilled or frozen.

facts.label: Initial incident period
facts.value: The first widely reported French disruption occurred overnight from October 11 to October 12, 2026; France's CERT-FR issued its initial alert on October 12 and last updated it on October 16.

facts.label: Location and expansion
facts.value: The initial known large-scale impact was in France. By November 2, supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia had also reported refrigeration or freezer disruptions described as apparent or suspected cyberattacks.

facts.label: Affected technology
facts.value: CERT-FR said it was aware of numerous compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC remote controllers and Copeland and Dixell xweb systems—equipment used to remotely manage refrigeration installations.

facts.label: Observed operational effect
facts.value: Reporting on the French incident described attackers changing refrigeration settings, including defrost programs, which raised temperatures and resulted in spoiled food; authorities also reported food losses and fires.

facts.label: Official response and attribution status
facts.value: CERT-FR warned that attack campaigns were probably still under way and advised removing exposed controllers from the public internet, using protected access such as a VPN, and updating or securely reconfiguring systems. As of November 2, public reporting had not identified a perpetrator or established that all affected countries' incidents were caused by the same actor.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the French onset and the reported European spillover through November 2, 2026; it does not by itself establish a single culprit, a definitive technical cause for every case, or the final financial, food-safety, and investigative outcomes.

event_overview.title: About US Midterm Elections
event_overview.subject: US Midterm Elections
event_overview.summary: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are nationwide federal elections held during a presidential term, principally to choose members of Congress. They also coincide with many state and local contests, whose offices, ballot questions, voting procedures and certification rules vary by jurisdiction.

facts.label: Election date
facts.value: Federal law sets congressional general elections for the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year; in 2026, that date is November 3.

facts.label: Congressional offices
facts.value: All House seats are regularly contested every two years because Representatives are chosen for two-year terms; Senate elections are staggered, with roughly one-third of senators facing election or reelection every two years.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: U.S. elections are decentralized: states set many of the rules for conducting and certifying elections, and counties, cities, townships or other local jurisdictions commonly administer voting. Federal law establishes certain nationwide requirements and standards.

facts.label: New congressional terms
facts.value: The members elected to the next Congress begin their terms at noon on January 3, 2027, under the Twentieth Amendment; the statutory election date refers to the Congress beginning the following January 3.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows developments tied to the 2026 midterm campaign and voting period, such as polling, early voting and party messaging; it does not aim to catalog every federal, state or local race, rule, result, recount or certification process.

event_overview.title: About Cybersecurity Incident
event_overview.subject: Cybersecurity Incident
event_overview.summary: This event is a series of suspected cyber intrusions into internet-connected commercial refrigeration controls, first reported in French food retail stores in mid-October 2026 and followed by similar disruptions elsewhere in Europe. The incidents caused refrigeration and freezer settings to change, forcing retailers to isolate equipment and discard food that could no longer be kept safely chilled or frozen.

facts.label: Initial incident period
facts.value: The first widely reported French disruption occurred overnight from October 11 to October 12, 2026; France's CERT-FR issued its initial alert on October 12 and last updated it on October 16.

facts.label: Location and expansion
facts.value: The initial known large-scale impact was in France. By November 2, supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia had also reported refrigeration or freezer disruptions described as apparent or suspected cyberattacks.

facts.label: Affected technology
facts.value: CERT-FR said it was aware of numerous compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC remote controllers and Copeland and Dixell xweb systems—equipment used to remotely manage refrigeration installations.

facts.label: Observed operational effect
facts.value: Reporting on the French incident described attackers changing refrigeration settings, including defrost programs, which raised temperatures and resulted in spoiled food; authorities also reported food losses and fires.

facts.label: Official response and attribution status
facts.value: CERT-FR warned that attack campaigns were probably still under way and advised removing exposed controllers from the public internet, using protected access such as a VPN, and updating or securely reconfiguring systems. As of November 2, public reporting had not identified a perpetrator or established that all affected countries' incidents were caused by the same actor.

event_overview.title: About US Midterm Elections
event_overview.subject: US Midterm Elections
event_overview.summary: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are nationwide federal elections held during a presidential term, principally to choose members of Congress. They also coincide with many state and local contests, whose offices, ballot questions, voting procedures and certification rules vary by jurisdiction.

facts.label: Election date
facts.value: Federal law sets congressional general elections for the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year; in 2026, that date is November 3.

facts.label: Congressional offices
facts.value: All House seats are regularly contested every two years because Representatives are chosen for two-year terms; Senate elections are staggered, with roughly one-third of senators facing election or reelection every two years.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: U.S. elections are decentralized: states set many of the rules for conducting and certifying elections, and counties, cities, townships or other local jurisdictions commonly administer voting. Federal law establishes certain nationwide requirements and standards.

facts.label: New congressional terms
facts.value: The members elected to the next Congress begin their terms at noon on January 3, 2027, under the Twentieth Amendment; the statutory election date refers to the Congress beginning the following January 3.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows developments tied to the 2026 midterm campaign and voting period, such as polling, early voting and party messaging; it does not aim to catalog every federal, state or local race, rule, result, recount or certification process.
